name: Scenicness of Listed Buildings in English Towns
description: Faithful replication: same task, scale and photographs as the paper (160 of the study's Geograph photographs of urban England, retrieved from Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0). Scenic-or-Not style rating: each participant sees 40 photographs, one at a time, drawn at random and balanced between photographs that contain a listed (legally protected historic) building and photographs without one, and rates "How scenic is this place?" from 1 (not scenic) to 10 (very scenic). The paper regresses each photograph's mean score on a listed-building dummy plus image-content controls and finds that listed buildings raise urban scenicness about as much as natural features. The page source holds each photograph's original Scenic-or-Not mean and variance, building type, prominence and Historic England list entry (from the authors' OSF data, osf.io/fcvmr), and the photographer is credited under every photo. Differences from the original study: (1) the paper analyses existing Scenic-or-Not ratings of 3,843 photographs; here 80 listed and 80 non-listed photographs are rated anew; (2) photographs where the listed building is marginal or obscured are left out; (3) a consent screen and one question (ever lived in the UK) are added. Cite: Sherborne & Malthouse (2026), Frontiers in Psychology 16: 1645424.
author: Sherborne & Malthouse

      '<div class="card"><div class="q">'+esc(Q.scenicness.title||'How scenic is this place?')+'</div><div class="scale">'+b+'</div><div class="ends"><span>1 · Not scenic</span><span>10 · Very scenic</span></div><div class="err"></div></div>';
    app.querySelectorAll('.scale button').forEach(function(x){x.onclick=function(){
      app.querySelectorAll('.scale button').forEach(function(y){y.disabled=true;});
      SPSite.answer('scenicness',Number(x.getAttribute('data-v')),{key:gid(f.name),shown:[f.name]}).then(function(r){if(!ok(r)){app.querySelectorAll('.scale button').forEach(function(y){y.disabled=false;});return err(r.error);}done[f.name]=true;window.scrollTo(0,0);next();});
    };});
  }
  function finish(){
    app.innerHTML='<h1>Thank you!</h1><div class="card"><p id="fin">Submitting…</p><div class="err"></div></div>';
    SPSite.complete().then(function(r){if(!ok(r)){err(r.error||'Some answers are missing.');setTimeout(function(){if((r.missing||[]).some(function(x){return x!=='scenicness';}))intro();else{done={};next();}},1800);}else{try{localStorage.removeItem('sherborne2025:list');}catch(e){}var s=document.getElementById('fin');if(s)s.textContent='Your ratings are saved.';}});
  }
  SPSite.onReady(function(ctx){
    ['consent','lived_in_uk','scenicness'].forEach(function(n){Q[n]=SPSite.getQuestion(n)||{};});
    files=(SPSite.getMedia('photos')||[]).filter(function(f){return /^[LN]\d*_?\d+\.(jpe?g|png)$/i.test(f.name)||/^[LN]/.test(f.name);});
    try{st=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('sherborne2025:list'));}catch(e){st=null;}
    if(!st||!Array.isArray(st.list)||!st.list.length||st.list.some(function(n){return !byName(n);}))st={list:draw()};
    try{localStorage.setItem('sherborne2025:list',JSON.stringify(st));}catch(e){}
    var a=(ctx&&ctx.answers)||{}, p=a.scenicness;
    (p&&Array.isArray(p.trials)?p.trials:[]).forEach(function(x){if(x&&x.value!=null){(x.shown||[]).forEach(function(n){done[n]=true;});}});
    if(a.consent===true)next();else intro();
  });
})();
</script>
